narrative: Material PL2__M5F2091E exhibits strongly intermittent demand with only 18.8% of working days carrying non-zero consumption and a CV of 2.48, indicating large, irregular order spikes typical of batch-pull or project-driven usage. Lead times, while short on average (1.40 WD), are highly unstable (CV 0.69) with occasional outliers exceeding 4 days. The combined demand-lead-time uncertainty produces a lead-time demand sigma of 3,326 units, driving the required safety stock to 5,471 units — 78% above the current SAP setting of 3,065. An (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 10,117 units is selected; the reorder point of 8,015 and safety lead time extension to 5.08 days together close the service-level gap at a marginal additional holding cost of ~$950/year.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) policy is appropriate for intermittent-lumpy demand because it triggers replenishment only when stock falls to the reorder point, avoiding unnecessary orders during the many zero-demand periods, while the fixed EOQ-derived quantity balances ordering and holding costs optimally given high annual volume.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (48,415 units) is not binding — post-replenishment peak stock of 15,588 units represents only 32% utilisation. No capacity-driven reduction was necessary.
